scope: Repair of the 14 findings left open by the first review of formal/mojo/, plus 5 new defects the repair surfaced.

headline_metric.note: Measured by a scanner that extracts every r.algebra(...) predicate, strips string literals, and reports arms whose remaining identifiers are empty or drawn only from the file's own comptime constants.

F3.defect: Eight of fifteen conjuncts in core_evo's live verdict, and four of six in monitoring_governance's, were handed the very constant they are compared against, so they were tautologies at runtime. core_evo's header claimed it 'feeds it a LIVE reading'; it fed seven.
F3.fix: Two conjuncts proved genuinely derivable and now are: castes counted from TaskRole in ecology/core_evolution.gleam (5), and a2ui counted from the three A2UI catalogs (core 15 + wave1 100 + wave2 124 = 239 ComponentSpec entries, the exact number previously passed as a literal). The remaining six -- modules, services, zenoh_topics, scc, canonical_broken and the 69-route requirement -- are recorded BLIND.
F3.declined_derivation: There are eight core_*.gleam files against a requiredServices of 8 and a requiredModules of 7. Selecting whichever count matches the expected number is the defect under repair, so no derivation was asserted for those. Stated here because declining is a judgement a reviewer should check.
F3.effect: Both oracles now report BLIND or WORLD_FAIL where they previously reported alignment. That is the honest verdict: they never measured those properties.

F4.defect: Thirteen arms matched colon-adjacent JSON by hand because these two files imported only Receipt/capture/contains, opting out of the three-valued readers the substrate made mandatory after the razr15 incident. core_evo was the sharpest: it detected presence with the whitespace-robust bare key and tested the value with the whitespace-fragile colon-adjacent form, so a pretty-printed endpoint yields presence=true and value=false -- a RECORDED WORLD FAILURE, not a BLIND.
F4.fix: Migrated to json_flag / json_int / json_signed / json_norm.
F4.surfaced_new_defect: json_signed had to be written. See new_defects.JSON_INT_NEGATIVE.

F5.defect: The header claimed the oracle 'renders the OTEL artifacts, and -- the part that matters -- CHECKS that the write landed instead of asserting it did'. There is no write in the file; the only world contact is test -d, wc -l and cat. The arms measured a file another process wrote at an unknown earlier time with no freshness check -- the observationNow defect relocated from a Lean constant to a filesystem artifact.
F5.fix: Header corrected to state the real division of labour; MAX_ARTIFACT_AGE_MIN bound added for both artifacts; the line-count arm gated on freshness so a correct count in a stale file is not evidence.

F6.defect: The algebra plane reproduced, from five comptime constants the oracle typed itself, the exact frozen-constant arithmetic (737 + 990 = 1727) that the file's own header condemns in the Lean twin. No arm read the twin. A corrected Lean census would have left every arm green. Separately, the measured-vs-declared delta was registered through r.world() -- which drives WORLD_FAIL and exit 1 -- three lines under a comment saying it is reported 'NOT as proof the model is wrong, because the census's original scope is unrecorded'.
F6.fix: All five declared values now read from the twin, so census:declared-total-is-consistent is a genuine differential between the twin's two records and the total its theorem asserts. The uncomparable delta moved to observe().

F9.defect: world_count(name, 0, 0) with no compiler invoked and no file read -- the arm was the literal 0 == 0, under a comment stating the criterion correctly. A sibling arm passed the literal True as value_ok, making it BLIND-or-PASS only. Two further arms (atlas08/atlas09) were identically true for every Int because the derived value cancelled out: the Mojo analogue of the G6 let _ := (a,b,c); true shape.
F9.fix: Compilability now read from the differential driver's durable receipt with an age bound and a non-empty-pairs gate; coverage report moved to observe(); the involution and no-fixed-point arms quantified over the four codes actually read from the ABI.
two_rejected_designs: Compiling 24 subjects inline: capture bounds every probe at timeout -k 5 20, so the arm would be killed and read BLIND on every run. An always-blind arm is no better than an always-passing one.

Enumerating subjects from the driver source: the driver content-discovers, so only ONE formal/lean path appears in it. That enumeration compiled a single file under a name claiming 'every differential subject' -- a weaker version of the same overclaim, caught only by checking the result against the name.

F10.defect: Two arms whose PASS condition required the defect to persist. twin_coverage's cover-blind-is-excluded-from-verified was v != (v + b), true iff b != 0: the moment the last blind subsystem exposed its evidence, algebra_failures would go to 1 and the receipt would report DIVERGENT -- the gravest verdict, meaning the model drifted from itself. Its name also described a disjointness property it never tested. language_conformance's arm passed only while the extensionless Bash surface exceeded the .sh surface, so converting that surface to OCaml would have made it a WORLD_FAIL.
F10.fix: Disjointness tested directly and holding vacuously when b = 0; blind count reported, never required nonzero; the undercount restated as an observation about the INSTRUMENT with the shell total reported rather than a floor asserted. Partition and fraction denominators switched from the literal 40 to the derived inventory; verified-fraction-percent renamed to per-mille, which is what it computed.

F11.defect: 28 of 123 algebra arms were literal tautologies, concentrated in nine files, with three files at 100% of their algebra plane: agent_profile 5/5, language_conformance 3/3, proof_plane_guard 6/6. Because status() returns VACUOUS when algebra_checks == 0, these arms existed to keep the counter above zero so the receipt could say PASS.
F11.worst_subclass: Arms whose NAME asserts a world fact the body never examines: prov:admitted-ev-ceiling-is-93 (93 == 93) read no contract; endpoint:gateway-port-matches-firewall-port (PORT == 8000) read no firewall; deploy-proved-total-fits-rtx2070maxq-8192mib had BOTH sides literal.
F11.second_order: proof_plane_guard's four lattice-* arms transcribed exit_of (the process exit-code table) while named for severity (the worst-wins lattice), and NO arm asserted WORLD_FAIL outranks BLIND -- the single ordering where the two tables disagree, and the one F7 showed status() was mishandling. The arm set covered everything except the thing that was wrong.
F11.fix: All 28 replaced with derived arms or, where the claim was not mathematical, deleted. The lattice is now read from the driver's severity table and the two tables are explicitly asserted to differ on the Blind/World_fail pair. Verified: 0 unfalsifiable arms remain of 129.
two_deletions_rather_than_rewrites: language_conformance's lang-rewriting-a-presence-check-preserves-it: the claim is about what file_exists MEANS and no arithmetic over a count expresses it. My first replacement was (presence_gates > 0) == (presence_gates != 0) -- a fresh tautology. The substantive test already existed as a world arm.

axis_registry's t6-parsing-correctly-is-not-rejecting: the comment said 'recorded as an observation' while the code registered an algebra arm holding True != False. Made an actual observation, as the comment always claimed.

F12.defect: Negative controls that pinned the subject's values into the instrument (declared == 101 and observed == 97; fpp_specs == 40). A legitimate change in the subject would fail the probe, set vacuous to 1, and make the receipt report VACUOUS -- which outranks everything -- so a reader sees 'the oracle cannot discriminate' when the truth is 'the subject moved and the oracle noticed'. If the measured quantity also changed, a genuine DIVERGENT would be OVERWRITTEN, because vacuity is tested first.
F12.fix: Probes test READABILITY and relational properties, not pinned values. The sibling probe abi-regime-parse-is-not-vacuous already showed the right shape in the same file.

F13.defect: Three argument-discard instances. allowlist_line(body, marker) carried a six-line docstring describing extraction logic over a body of `return body`, ignored marker entirely, and was DEAD -- and had it been called it would have handed both dialect paths the same whole-file body, collapsing the two-dialect model its header says the correction was for. twin_coverage had the literal `_ = occurrences(ids, String("l"))`. language_conformance computed `executors` and never checked or printed it, while the comment beside it stated 'nothing in the tree executes it' AS A FINDING.
F13.fix: Dead function deleted (safe because the call-site grep found only its definition); the discarded occurrences call removed rather than wired to an invented use; the executors finding promoted to an arm, which now fails -- the twin asserts a systemd stratum with no invoker.

F14.defect: Arms using bare world() where a missing instrument became an outage or a missing subject became a pass. Both directions present: four port arms per oracle manufacturing outages when ss is absent (and ss is not a preflight-pinned toolchain), and legacy-name / toml-only-name arms concluding a clean world from no configs at all.
F14.fix: Converted to world_or_blind with the instrument's own availability as the presence predicate. Remaining bare world() calls were audited: one, inside an existing readings_complete guard, is correct.

F15.defect: 52 observe() calls fed String(an_int) could never register BLIND, because observe detects blindness by raw.byte_length() == 0 and String(-1) is two characters -- while -1 is the sentinel every count() helper returns for 'could not read'. A receipt could report observations: 3, blind: 0 when all three greps had failed.
F15.fix: New Receipt.observe_int treats a negative as uncountable; 61 call sites migrated mechanically and compile-checked. 11 composite observes (a + b concatenations) were left: they are multi-valued strings rather than a single count, and converting them would require splitting each into separate arms.
F15.self_inflicted_followup: observe_int was then used for a legitimately negative value (the -3 SQL trap code) and reported a correctly-read value as BLIND. The absence/negative collision one layer up from the json_int bug. Fixed by using observe() with a string for signed codes.

F16.defect: The 'declared count' was a hardcoded 11 dressed as a derivation: the contract writes the figure as the WORD 'Eleven', so the inner digit grep matched nothing, exited non-zero, and `|| echo 11` supplied the literal -- with a second `if contract_claim < 0: contract_claim = 11` behind it. Both fallbacks landed on 11. Correcting the contract in prose to 'Thirty-six records carry...' would match neither alternation, fall back to 11 again, and leave the arm failing: remediation could not clear the check.
F16.fix: The number-word is parsed with no numeric fallback. If the contract says something the table does not cover, the declared side is unreadable and the arm is BLIND. Currently reports got-37-want-11, which is the real stale-contract finding.

F17.defect: Stale and fragile instruments: a raw tailnet IP (reassignable, and barred by the FQDN mandate); probes passing when the node was DOWN, because curl prints 000 on connection failure, which is non-empty and != 200; a wrong-model-id probe satisfied by an EMPTY listing; a crashpad arm passing on a TIMEOUT, since not contains("", ...) is true; inner timeout wrappers (30s, 40s, 20s) dead under capture's own timeout -k 5 20, so a reader would believe a bound that could not apply.
F17.fix: FQDN substituted after verifying it answers 200, not after. 000 excluded explicitly and the absent-path probe additionally requires a real path to have served on the same run, so the refusal is evidence about routing rather than reachability. The listing probe requires the canonical id to be present. The crashpad arm requires the run to have completed. Inner bounds removed or lowered under the capture budget so the inner tool reports its own timeout.

F18.defect: Name/body mismatches and channel errors: world_json and world_count omitted the 'world:' prefix their siblings apply, so an outage was indistinguishable from an algebra divergence in the detail field; bml06:lyapunov-chain-is-monotone tested three equalities and never compared the values to each other; atlas06-...-disagree-everywhere checked 2 of 4 regimes; analytics-declares-twelve-catalog-targets tested the presence of a KEY NAME, not the number twelve; verified-fraction-percent held per-mille; json_int truncates floats silently; two agent_profile arms graded grep -c '<theorem name>' as 'proved'; three more compared a grep LINE COUNT against the AGENT COUNT.
F18.fix: Prefix added; monotonicity tested relationally alongside the value-reproduction arm, which is the real differential; all four regimes included; the catalog value read and compared; unit put in the name; truncation documented; the presence arms renamed to say 'declared' and backed by a second arm reading the differential receipt, so presence and elaboration are two claims in two arms; the three category-error arms converted to BLIND with the line counts reported as observations, and the summary's met/total split into met-of-measurable so an unmeasured obligation is not counted as an unmet one.

JSON_INT_NEGATIVE.defect: json_int accumulates ASCII digits and stops at the first non-digit, so a leading minus terminates the scan immediately and EVERY negative field reads as -1, which the helper reserves for ABSENT. Its own docstring stated the precondition: 'No UOS telemetry field is negative; if one ever is, this helper must gain a separate presence result rather than guess.' That precondition is false, and the mandate says so: CLAUDE.md mandate 1 defines the fail-closed interception codes as embedded NUL -2 and raw SQL -3, and bionic_interception_oracle reads adversarial_sqli_trap_code: -3. The substrate could not read the very codes the policy requires to exist.
JSON_INT_NEGATIVE.found_by: Migrating bionic's hand-rolled matches onto the three-valued readers under F4. The arm went BLIND, and the blindness was the reader's, not the subject's.
JSON_INT_NEGATIVE.fix: json_signed (signed parse, 0 on absence) plus json_has (presence asked separately), so absence and a negative value stay distinct. Callers pair them through world_or_blind.

LEDGER_ATTRIBUTION.defect: 11 of 48 verified_by check attributions credited an oracle that does not contain the named check. twin_coverage's phantom detector matched names against the UNION of all oracles -- a choice its own comment defends, correctly, for EXISTENCE -- so cross-oracle misattribution was invisible to it. But an entry claims 'verified_by oracle X via check C'; if C lives in oracle Y the claim is false even though C exists, and nobody ever confirmed X covers that subsystem. Most cases were the same probe implemented twice under different names (cockpit-4100 vs cockpit-http-4100) with the ledger merging two oracles' checks into one block.
LEDGER_ATTRIBUTION.fix: verified_by is now a list of per-oracle blocks naming only checks that oracle contains. One check was withdrawn entirely (see WITHDRAWN_CHECK). twin_coverage gained every-claimed-check-is-in-the-oracle-credited, which fails on any future misattribution. Two amendments were needed: the second because later renames in razr15 invalidated two more attributions -- a rename that STRENGTHENS a check still breaks every artifact citing it by name, and the new arm is what caught it.

WITHDRAWN_CHECK.what: census-matches-declared-under-stated-scope was withdrawn, not renamed. It asserted the measured corpus must equal the declared census, which F6 established is not assertable because the census's original scope is unrecorded. That entry now rests on three checks, not four.
WITHDRAWN_CHECK.note: Coverage evidence there is WEAKER than the ledger previously recorded. Stated plainly rather than papered over, because the alternative is keeping a claim the oracle has just said it cannot establish.

STALE_INSTRUMENT_PROF09.defect: The oracle grepped THM_PROF_09_all_intelligence_values_conform, a name the subject does not contain: PROF-09 was restated earlier as THM_PROF_09_conformance_is_insensitive_to_intelligence. The arm reported got-0-want-1 -- 'the optionality proof is missing' -- when the proof was present under its current name. A false negative from the instrument, indistinguishable in the receipt from a real gap.
STALE_INSTRUMENT_PROF09.fix: Matched on the stable THM_PROF_09 prefix so a future restatement of the suffix cannot blind it.

VACUOUS_BY_EMPTY_PIPELINE.defect: The ledger-attribution arm I had just added matched '"oracle": "X", "checks": [...]' on a single line. Re-serialising the ledger with indentation made the pattern match NOTHING, so the pipeline emitted no 'bad' lines, wc -l returned 0, and THE ARM PASSED BY SEEING NOTHING -- on the very run that broke it.
VACUOUS_BY_EMPTY_PIPELINE.fix: Extraction whitespace-normalised (the F4 lesson applied to a local artifact), and both arms gated on having extracted a non-zero number of attributions, so an extraction failure is BLIND and never a pass. Verified non-vacuous: 17 attribution blocks and 48 check names extracted; a planted misattribution is detected.

withdrawn_by_author_on_inspection: My replacement for context_path_kpi's `200 >= 100` asserted that span_within_budget REJECTS an inverted p99/observed pair. It went DIVERGENT and the PREDICATE WAS RIGHT: Lean :141 constrains only observedNs <= budgetNs and p99Ns <= budgetNs, nothing about their order. The Mojo mirror is faithful; I had invented a requirement neither plane makes and called the mirror wrong for not meeting it. Replaced with an arm testing what the predicate genuinely constrains, and the ordering gap recorded as an unconstrained property on both planes.

differential.divergent_cause: pre-existing dual-encoding parity divergences (regime and archetype integer encodings, and the cascade index-1 disagreement) that are OPERATOR DECISIONS, not repairable by an oracle
differential.verdict_direction: Several oracles moved from PASS to BLIND or WORLD_FAIL. That is the intended direction: the repairs removed arms that could not fail and replaced them with arms that can, or with an explicit BLIND where the instrument cannot see.

reviewers.detail: Exit 0 on all three attempts across two prompt shapes, including one explicitly instructing it to skip the MCP/KM preamble. The first two terminated after KM-triad lookups having read no file; the third produced no response block at all, ending immediately after the SessionStart hooks. Recorded so the review is never credited to two reviewers. This is a reproducible local Codex failure, not a prompting problem, and it is an open environment issue.

reviewers.outcome: commissioned for the re-review of all 17 files

unreviewed.note: A 17th oracle, written by ANOTHER WRITER during this session (mtime 56 seconds after an unrelated edit of mine; a Lean twin UosProvenanceCeilingAndImpactTwin.lean appeared alongside it). At the moment it was first compiled it imported three symbols the substrate does not export and could not run, which is why the differential reported 14 pairs rather than 15. It now compiles and reports PASS. It was not in the first review's inventory of 16 and has never been reviewed. Left untouched: another writer owns it.

footer: Document and component evidence do not grant system admission. Sa-plan remains the sole execution authority. EV ceiling 93; EV-94..109 NOT_ADMITTED.

SUPERSEDED_BY_REREVIEW.reviewer: local-claude-agent, max effort, 17 files read in full, 7 oracles executed
SUPERSEDED_BY_REREVIEW.verdict: This record OVERSTATES the repair. Read it alongside the re-review.

corrections_to_this_record.detail: The count of LITERAL tautologies is 0 and that was verified. But three replacements are STRUCTURALLY unfalsifiable, which my scanner could not see because they reference a derived variable that cancels out. ontology_atlas atlas06 is `x != 3 - x`, i.e. 2x != 3, which has no integer solution; atlas08 is `3-(3-x) == x`; atlas09 is `(3-x) != x`, true because 3 is odd. Executed over x in [-500,500]: zero falsifying inputs for all three. My F18 fix WIDENED atlas06 from two regimes to four, and my F9 comment in the same file says verbatim "BOTH ARE IDENTICALLY TRUE FOR EVERY Int" about two of them. I wrote that sentence and then re-expressed the same expressions.

corrections_to_this_record.claim: "F3 ... castes counted from TaskRole in ecology/core_evolution.gleam (5)"
corrections_to_this_record.detail: The subject's casteCount means the five-caste holarchy. core_hive.gleam declares `pub type HiveCaste` with EXACTLY the five names Lean holarchyCastes declares -- QueenConductor, ForagerBuilder, NurseDiagnostician, ArchitectSynthesizer, SovereignSentinel -- and caste_wip_limit gives 1,4,2,2,2 summing to 11, matching THM_ONT_05 exactly. TaskRole (ImplRole, RcaTpsRole, SovereignGateRole, FmeaFormalRole, ConductorRole) shares ONLY its cardinality of 5. I picked a carrier because its NUMBER matched -- the exact defect this record congratulates itself for declining on requiredServices. Adding a sixth TaskRole reports a false divergence; removing a caste from HiveCaste reports nothing.

corrections_to_this_record.claim: "F6 ... now read from the twin, making it a real differential" and the uncomparable-scope rationale
corrections_to_this_record.detail: km_census asserts in three places that the census scope "is not recorded anywhere in the file and cannot be recovered". The scope IS recorded, three lines above the two `def` lines the oracle greps: "Independent census over AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, docs/**, contracts/**, measured 2026-11-05T16:44Z." Measured under the declared scope: wiki 1492, zk 1867 against declared 1015/1308 -- a +47%/+43% drift, fully comparable. I used the false unrecoverability claim to downgrade a genuine world_count to an unfalsifiable observe, and the pair now reads PASS over a half-fold drift.

corrections_to_this_record.claim: "withdrawn_by_author_on_inspection: the ordering is an unconstrained property on both planes"
corrections_to_this_record.detail: THM_KPI_06_monotonic_span_timings at UosContextPathKpiOtelTwin.lean:158-159 proves `observedNs <= p99Ns && p99Ns <= budgetNs` by decide. spanWithinBudget does not constrain the ordering; the TWIN does, in a separate theorem, and THM_KPI_06 has no Mojo counterpart at all. So I corrected a correct instinct into an error, and recorded the error as a correction. The replacement arm is additionally a byte-identical duplicate of an existing arm in the same file.

corrections_to_this_record.claim: "F9 ... compilability now read from the differential receipt" / "F18 ... backed by a second arm reading the differential receipt"
corrections_to_this_record.status: BOTH PASS BY NOT FINDING EVIDENCE
corrections_to_this_record.detail: The receipt is append-only and its newest line is whatever ran last. A --pair run writes `"pairs":1`. Both arms grep the newest line for their own subject and pass when it is absent, gated only on pairs > 0 and age <= 24h. Verified: the last three lines are pairs 15, pairs 1, pairs 1. ontology_atlas already computes differential_subjects = 26 and does not use it in the gate. The arm named "every-differential-subject-is-compilable" passes from a one-pair receipt -- the same overclaim its own comment rejects an earlier design for.

corrections_to_this_record.claim: "F8 ... positive control kept, as an observation where it belongs"
corrections_to_this_record.status: THE CONTROL WAS DISSOLVED, NOT RELOCATED
corrections_to_this_record.detail: observe(name, String(Bool)) is never empty and therefore never BLIND and never failing. Four positive controls were moved from a channel that can fail into one that cannot. In each case the real positive assertion survives only because a separate algebra arm happens to exist.

The replacement algebra arm `sh_files + bare_bash > sh_files` reduces to `bare_bash > 0`. Converting the 39 extensionless Bash scripts to OCaml -- the policy requirement this oracle exists to motivate -- makes it `7 > 7`, an algebra failure, i.e. DIVERGENT, in a file where it is the ONLY algebra arm. I moved an inverted-polarity check from the world channel to the algebra channel, where the substrate documents failure as "the model drifted from itself ... must never be reported as an ordinary outage".

corrections_to_this_record.claim: differential tally "6 PASS / 1 BLIND / 6 WORLD_FAIL / 2 DIVERGENT"
corrections_to_this_record.detail: Independent reproduction: 7 PASS / 1 BLIND / 5 WORLD_FAIL / 2 DIVERGENT. Of the two DIVERGENT, axis_registry T3 is legitimate (Tier1Rete vs Tier1Compress). bionic_interception is MANUFACTURED: its three parity arms require the regime and archetype encodings to AGREE, while THM_ATLAS_06 proves they disagree everywhere and THM_ATLAS_11 proves the sole archetype agreement is prose -- and ontology_atlas mirrors both and PASSES. The oracle set reports "the encodings disagree" = PASS and "the encodings must agree" = DIVERGENT about the same two facts. Exactly one can ever be green; no change to the tree makes both pass.

SUPERSEDED_BY_REREVIEW.pattern: The repair pass diagnosed an anti-pattern and then committed it in the same sitting, repeatedly and in writing: it condemned "picking whichever count matches the expected number" and picked TaskRole for its cardinality; it wrote "BOTH ARE IDENTICALLY TRUE FOR EVERY Int" and re-expressed both; it rejected an enumeration for overclaiming "every subject" and reproduced the overclaim through a receipt; it named the VACUOUS-on-legitimate-change anti-pattern in agent_profile and introduced it in razr15. The scanner I used to certify "0 tautologies" could only see literals, so it certified exactly the class I had been measuring and missed the class I had created.
